title: Paramartha Guru Tale 81 (简体中文)

full_text:
On a scorching summer day, when the sun reached its absolute zenith in the heavens, Guru Paramartha and his disciples were traveling across an open, treeless plain with their faithful gray donkey.

The heat was oppressive, and the sun beat straight down from the middle of the sky.

Matti happened to look beneath the donkey's belly. Because the sun was directly overhead, the donkey's shadow was compressed into a tiny, four-inch patch directly beneath its hooves, completely hidden by its body!

Matti shrieked in horror: 'MASTER! A DEMONIC CALAMITY! OUR NOBLE DONKEY HAS LOST HIS SHADOW!'

The Guru and disciples halted. They walked around the beast: from the left, no shadow; from the right, no shadow; from behind, no shadow!

Madayan turned pale with astrological dread: 'In occult treatises, when a living creature loses its shadow, it signifies that its soul has been stolen by the Lord of Death! Within three hours, the beast will turn into a zombie and bite our throats!'

The Guru was terrified: 'How can the shadow be restored to its rightful owner?'

Madayan expounded his Shadow Reattachment Ceremony: 'We must supply the beast with an artificial shadow until his natural shadow returns from the other world! We will drape five black woolen blankets over his back, tie them beneath his belly, and hang black umbrellas from his ears!'

The disciples draped five heavy, suffocating black horse blankets over the poor donkey, tied them with ropes, and opened two black umbrellas, tying them to the animal's halter.

The temperature beneath the five black blankets under the blazing noon sun reached boiling point!

The suffocating, sweating donkey stood for three minutes, his eyes rolling in frantic distress.

Then, with an enraged, desperate bray of rebellion, the beast kicked out with all four hooves, bucked like a mad bull, threw off the black blankets, trampled the umbrellas to splinters, and bolted across the plain toward a shady banyan tree half a mile away!

Standing beneath the spreading banyan boughs, where cool shade covered the earth, the donkey stopped, panting contentedly.

The disciples ran across the field, arriving out of breath.

Looking beneath the tree, Matti saw a massive, cool, dark shadow spreading twenty yards around the beast!

Matti cheered in ecstatic triumph: 'A MIRACLE! THE SHADOW HAS RETURNED! AND IT HAS GROWN TWENTY TIMES LARGER THAN BEFORE!'

Guru Paramartha stroked the donkey's nose with deep reverence: 'Our blankets have cured his soul; behold the magnificent expansion of his shadow!'
moral: Looking for an animal's shadow at high noon makes you believe the beast has lost its soul. [ZH]
